- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is significantly below recent history, adjust upward by 1–2% to account for bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.4) and forecast is above recent history, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction to bearish signals.  
- If forecast shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the immediate post-spike values by 3–5% to correct for overshoot.  
- If true outcome consistently lags forecast by 3–5 days, apply a 1–2% downward correction to the 30-day forecast to align with mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings) and forecast is smooth, introduce a 1–3% smoothing penalty to avoid overfitting to sentiment noise.
